changes.text: [new] Management overhaul: investments and products got a lot deeper
sub: Investments can now be cashed out — enter what you actually received and only the profit (or loss) beyond your original principal is logged, so a $300 investment cashed out for $350 shows $50 earned, not $350
Cash-outs can be edited afterward, and deleting one reverts the investment to "not yet cashed out" — exactly as if it never happened
Products can log repeatable returns — early returns recoup the product's cost first, and only the excess counts as profit
Products can carry an optional date, which keeps a matching entry on your calendar in sync automatically
Product and transaction notes are no longer shown inline in the list — click a row to view its full details instead

changes.text: [new] Budgets: set spending limits for any timeframe, not just monthly
sub: Add as many budgets as you want — Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly, or a custom date range
Each one can optionally be scoped to a single category, e.g. a "Marketing" budget that only tracks Marketing expenses
Weekly/Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly budgets automatically roll into the current period — no recreating them
A new Breakdown view groups income, expenses, and investments by category with totals and percentages
"Balance" is now labeled "Wallet" to make clear it's your net take-home, not a running transaction total

changes.text: [new] Project types: tell Notebook what a project is for
sub: Six presets to start from — Blank, Novel/Story, Worldbuilding/Campaign, Screenplay, Poetry/Collection, and Product/Professional work — each with sensible defaults for what's visible
Save your own custom presets from any project's current setup, reusable when creating new ones
Picking a type is part of creating a new project now, and can be changed later from Settings

changes.text: [new] Sidebar rooms and Home tiles/sections are now per-project
sub: Previously these were shared across every project — a Poetry project and a Worldbuilding project always looked identical. Each project now remembers its own visibility
Appearance settings (theme, accent color, density, etc.) are unaffected and still apply everywhere, since those aren't about content
A new "This project" group at the top holds everything scoped to the current project — Project type and Library
Every category is now a full-width row with a real description of what it does, instead of a cramped icon grid with little to no explanation
Home tiles now pull their icon and label directly from the sidebar, so they can't drift out of sync (e.g. a tile silently still saying "Timer" after the room was renamed "Productivity")

changes: [new] Ctrl/Cmd+S now exports a full backup instead of just forcing an immediate autosave

changes.text: [fix] Patch notes could fail to show what a version actually changed
sub: Caused by the app's own version number not being bumped to match the published changelog — fixed, and a console warning now flags it early if it happens again

changes: [fix] Budgets and products weren't included in full JSON exports or selective snapshot restores — they are now
[new] Patch notes now support tags, and lines can be broken down into a sub-bullet list — see this entry's format for an example

changes.text: [new] Management: a new sidebar room for real-world budgeting and product tracking, shared across every project like Productivity
sub: Budget: log income and expenses with category, amount, date, and notes — running income/expense/balance summary
Products: track what you're building through a status pipeline (Idea, Planned, Active, Done)
A Management tile on Home shows your current budget balance

changes.text: [new] In-world economy tracking, integrated into Entries
sub: New Product entry type for fictional goods/items
Added a Wealth field to Characters and a Treasury field to Factions

changes.text: [fix] Rest tokens were accumulating far too fast
sub: New rate: 1 token for hitting your weekly goal, +1 for clearing the overachieve challenge — roughly 1-2 a week if you're working
Medals no longer hand out tokens on their own; they're celebration-only now
Existing save stockpiles are recalculated once, automatically, on next load

changes: [fix] Home tiles now come from a single registry, so they can't drift out of sync with the sidebar
[redesign] Multiple Productivity tabs have been given touch-ups

_comment_tags: Changelog lines can start with a bracketed tag, e.g. "[bug] Fixed the thing".
This key is documentation only — the app never reads it, just 'version' and 'changelog' above.
[new] / [feature] / [added]                       -> New (sage)
[bug] / [fix] / [fixed] / [bugfix]                 -> Bug (red)
[security]                                         -> Security (red)
[redesign] / [redesigned]                          -> Redesign (purple)
[rework] / [reworked]                              -> Rework (amber)
[improvement] / [improved] / [perf] / [performance]-> Improved (blue)
[removed]                                          -> Removed (neutral)
[deprecated]                                       -> Deprecated (neutral)
Any other bracketed word -> still renders as a neutral pill, title-cased.
No brackets at all -> plain untagged line.
Tags are case-insensitive and only match at the very start of the line.
Each entry in 'changes' can also be an object instead of a plain string,
to break one tagged line down into specifics:
{ "text": "[fix] Tokens accumulating rapidly", "sub": ["detail one", "detail two"] }
'text' follows the same [tag] + markdown rules as a plain-string line.
'sub' is a list of plain strings, rendered as a smaller nested bullet list
underneath — each one also supports its own [tag] and markdown if needed,
though that's rarely necessary for a sub-bullet.
